title: Rotation in the NGC 1333 IRAS 4C Outflow
question: Does the IRAS 4C molecular outflow rotate, and what do its angular momentum and launching radii imply for the launching mechanism (X-wind vs disk wind)?

data.angular_resolution: continuum 0.65" x 0.41" (PA -6.8 deg); lines in Table 1

what.value: Line frequencies and parameters from CDMS

evidence.quote: Information taken from the CDMS database ((cite: Muller05))

what.value: Inclination about 25 deg from Segura-Cox et al.

evidence.quote: to about $25^\circ$ between the disk plane and the line of sight ((cite: SeguraCox16))

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image continuum and line data
recipe.method: CASA calibration, phase+amplitude self-cal on continuum applied to lines, CLEAN imaging
Total flux above 3 sigma within 2" converted to mass

recipe.goal: Measure outflow rotation and specific angular momentum from PV cuts
recipe.method: PV cuts perpendicular to the outflow axis at each z; locate emission peaks of northern and southern walls; derive R_out, V_rot, j=R_out V_rot
key_parameters: cuts 0.5" wide, z=+0.5" to +6" (east), peaks defined as 0.9x peak intensity, PA of axis 96 deg

recipe.goal: Derive launching radius and magnetic lever arm
recipe.method: Anderson03 method using R_out, V_rot, V_p, protostar mass; lever arm from Ferreira06
CS highest velocity/position (method 1) and SO outer radius and max velocity (method 2) in mid-plane PV diagrams; M=V^2R/(2G)
assumptions: CS traces envelope outside barrier; SO enhanced at barrier

answer_key.quantity: Mean specific angular momentum of outflow

evidence.quote: The mean value of the specific angular momentum is about 100 $\mbox{au km s}^{-1}$ with a standard deviation of 40 $\mbox{au km s}^{-1}$.
The position angle of this outflow axis is 96$^\circ$
from about 0.5 $\mbox{km s}^{-1}$ at $z=0.5\ensuremath{''}$ (120 au) to about 0.1 $\mbox{km s}^{-1}$ at $z=6\ensuremath{''}$ (1400 au)
with a mean value of about 7.5 $\mbox{km s}^{-1}$ and standard deviation of 0.07 $\mbox{km s}^{-1}$
mean value of 15 au and a standard deviation of 7 au for the case of $V_p=3~\mbox{km s}^{-1}$
a mean value of 5.6 au and a standard deviation of 1.8 au for the case of $V_p=10~\mbox{km s}^{-1}$
The total continuum flux above $3\sigma$ within a radius of 2$\ensuremath{''}$ is 95 mJy
which corresponds to a mass of 0.061 $M_\odot$
which gives $V_\mathrm{CB1}=2.5~\mbox{km s}^{-1}$ and $R_\mathrm{CB1}=0.2\ensuremath{''}$, i.e. 50 au

score_reason: Data and many settings are given, but the CASA version, self-cal details and manual peak-picking are unspecified; the analysis is simple and numeric.
rediscovery_reason: The archival ALMA data are linked to the paper, the recipe (imaging, PV cuts, formulas) is mostly specified, and the results are numeric.
